newsitem.title: GERMANY: Still buoyant German shares open at new highs.
newsitem.headline: Still buoyant German shares open at new highs.

text.p: German shares opened at new record-highs on Monday, continuing to gain inspiration from last Friday's surge in the dollar and Wall Street shares, with expectations of new heights later in the day.
The DAX index of Germany's leading 30 blue chip shares stood 27.50 points, or 1.06 percent, higher at 2,623.46 in early bourse trade, cruising past the 2,600 threshold for the first time.
The advance was largely a delayed reaction to a U.S. rally later on Friday after economic data interpreted as easing U.S. rate hike fears, and was seen as having further to go.
"It looks as if the (German) market wants to keep going higher and few believe the gains will stop for now," one trader said.
Strong international buying interest from fund managers was cited and traders said improved trading volumes would underpin the market.

Shortcovering of "sell" positions on September DAX futures contracts, which expire later this week, was also seen as helping the market higher. September DAX futures traded 7.5 points higher at 2,622.5 in mid-morning dealings.
Some traders said some profit-taking would emerge during the session but that the DAX was not showing signs of wavering and that Wall Street would still drive the market's movements.

Among specific shares, chemical concern Bayer AG traded just over a mark higher at 55.90 as it refused to comment on a newspaper report that it was launching a U.S. joint venture, but said it would be making a statement later in the day.
The New York Times had earlier reported that it planned to start a joint venture with Roche Holding Ltd in the U.S to sell Roche's Aleve analgesic and other products.
